listings.description: The Running Springs Area Chamber of Commerce Certified Farmers Market and Artisan Faire runs every Saturday, April 25 - November 21 (the Saturday before Thanksgiving), 9am-1pm. Enjoy a wide variety of Vegetables & Fruit, Herbs, Cage-Free Eggs, Fresh Bread, Jam, Coffee, Mexican Food, Food Artisans, Sweets, Art, Products, Clothing, Body Products, Jewelry, Nonprofit information, and Live Music. Updates are posted on Facebook & Twitter @RSfarmersmarket or Instagram @RS_farmersmarket. The market is nestled between a very nice playground, picnic tables, and the Running Springs Branch Library at 2645 Whispering Pines Drive. At 6,000 feet elevation, the field has nice views of nearby pine trees, blue skies (mostly) and cooler mountain temperatures. The area is considered a Gateway to the San Bernardino Mountains. listings.name: Millen Produce Market
listings.description: Millen Produce Market is your local destination for fresh, homemade, and homegrown goodness right in the heart of our community. Each week, you’ll find an abundance of farm-fresh vegetables picked at their peak. From juicy tomatoes and crisp cucumbers to seasonal favorites like squash, okra, and sweet corn, our farmers bring the very best of the garden straight to you. Alongside produce, the market showcases a variety of homemade goods made with care and tradition. Local kitchens stock tables with delicious baked treats—cakes, cookies, breads, and pies—that capture the warmth of home cooking. For those who love classic Southern flavors, shelves of jams, jellies, and preserves are filled with the tastes of summer in a jar, ready to sweeten your mornings or make the perfect gift. No visit would be complete without sampling Georgia’s favorite snack—hot, salty boiled peanuts. Freshly cooked and seasoned, they’re the perfect companion while you browse the market.

A standout feature is the Young Entrepreneurs Market, a dedicated space for kids under 16 to launch and run their mini businesses. listings.description: The Mount Carroll Farmers Market is held every Saturday from 8 a.m. to noon, starting Memorial Day weekend and running through Halloween. Located in the heart of historic downtown Mount Carroll, IL, the market is set against the charming backdrop of the town's red brick streets and Market Square. Each week, you can shop for a diverse selection of fresh, locally grown produce, homemade baked goods, handcrafted items, specialty crops, and more. Enjoy a lively, family-friendly atmosphere with live local music and opportunities to connect with farmers and artisans. It's a great way to support the local economy while enjoying high-quality, fresh, and affordable products. The market is on the north side of the Carroll County Courthouse Square, just off Route 78, making it a central hub for small-town charm and local goods.

listings.description: Common Ground Producers and Growers is a mobile farmers market and food hub. It is a family-run agricultural organization based in Wichita, Kansas, operating the state’s longest-running Mobile farmers market and food hub. Founded in 2014 by multi-generational farmer and CEO Donna Pearson McClish, the organization was established to eliminate food insecurity by delivering fresh, locally grown produce directly into neighborhoods with limited access to healthy food. Guided by the motto “All are fed. No one is hungry.” Common Ground operates on Pearson’s Family Farms—the largest Black-owned urban farm in the region. On the farm, Common Ground aggregates, processes, and distributes Kansas-grown fruits and vegetables sourced from more than 40 farmers statewide. The mobile farmers market and food hub currently serves 37 locations across 10 cities and 4 counties, while ensuring equitable compensation for farmers and maintaining affordable prices for customers.

listings.description: Founded in 1919, and operating from our current location since 1930, our 106 year old market is the second oldest continuously operating public market in the state of Michigan. Ann Arbor Farmers Market is also open twice daily in May-December, and on Saturdays year-round. We accept 5 different food assistance programs, and have the highest amount of food assistance dollars spent at our market as compared to other farmers markets in Washtenaw County. We host special events like Cooking Demos, Food Truck Rallies, and Flower Day, and have prepared food, live music, and community groups regularly throughout our market season. We are run by the the City of Ann Arbor Parks and Recreation Department. As we are a City park, others rent our space for events like the Sunday Artisan Market, Kindlefest, Ann Arbor Asian Night Market, The Local Food Festival, and more.

We are 4 blocks from the Blake Transit station and there are multiple parking lots as well as street parking available within walking distance.

listings.description: Uptown Farmers Market was launched in 2020 in center city Charlotte with a mission to engage our neighbors around locally grown fresh foods to support local farmers and food artisans, educate on nutrition, and eliminate food insecurity in the Charlotte community. As a producer-only market, it supports over 60 approved vendors selling fruits and vegetables, pasture-raised meats, baked goods and other artisan foods, eggs, honey, flowers and plants, and natural skincare. Each week the Market hosts musicians, a food truck, children's activities, and cooking demos. The Market is a USDA retailer and provides Double Bucks weekly for SNAP users, and Triple Bucks once per month. The Market runs a senior shuttle program and is a host market for the NC Senior Farmers Market voucher program. Open every Saturday, 8:00am - 12:30pm during the primary season of April-December, and 10:00am - 12:00pm during the winter season January-March. Free parking, pet friendly.

We provide easy access to food produced in Cleveland County and the surrounding 50 miles, and are proud to showcase the family-owned farms and small businesses in our region. Our vendors have deep roots in the rolling soils of the North Carolina Foothills, producing an astonishing array of fresh fruits & vegetables, meat & poultry products, baked goods, artisan cheeses, honey, nuts, herbs and other specialty food items. listings.name: Cuyahoga Valley WINTER Farmers Market
listings.description: Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets’ (CVFM) works to provide access to and education about sustainable foods and agriculture to the communities in Northeast Ohio by building connections between our community with the producers of locally grown food. CVFM was established in 2022 to continue the operation of the long-running Countryside farmers markets in Howe Meadow and at Old Trail School, both located in the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. These vibrant farmers markets have been in operation since 2004 and have been growing steadily since their inception. CVFM MARKET IMPACT: During our Summer market in Howe Meadow (May-October) we connect on average 2,500 (peak 3,000) members of our community to producers of local food. During our Winter market at Old Trail School (November-April) we have on average 600 shoppers per market (peak 1,000). Provide consistent sales outlet for 70 local farms and businesses.
listings.locationNote: The winter market continues to bring you fresh, local goodness even when the weather turns chilly. listings.description: The Dane Coun­ty Farm­ers’ Mar­ket on the Square is a Sat­ur­day and Wednes­day tra­di­tion in Madi­son, Wis­con­sin. You’ll find the season’s best boun­ty of veg­eta­bles, flow­ers, meats, cheeses, and spe­cial­ty prod­ucts from approx­i­mate­ly 220 ven­dors through­out the year. Over 130 mem­bers attend every Sat­ur­day. All of the items for sale are grown, raised, and pro­duced in Wis­con­sin by the per­son behind the stand.
listings.locationNote: The Sat­ur­day Dane Coun­ty Farm­ers’ Mar­ket is con­ve­nient­ly locat­ed on the tree-lined grounds sur­round­ing the Wis­con­sin State Capi­tol build­ing — oth­er­wise known as ​“the Square” — in down­town Madi­son, Wisconsin. As a pro­duc­er-only farm­ers’ mar­ket, our ven­dors are lim­it­ed by their pro­duc­tion and har­vest yields. This means that they may sell out before the close of Mar­ket. Please vis­it the Mar­ket ear­ly for the best experience. Grab your fam­i­ly, friends, and your reusable shop­ping bags and enjoy a Madi­son tradition!
